key_insight: Two-frequency cylinder oscillations create controllable asymmetric steady streaming, and the resulting pumping strength depends strongly on the amplitude ratio and phase difference.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tunable mechanism for microfluidic pumping in lab-on-a-chip devices, with force on an annulus serving as a practical proxy for net channel flux.
method: Reduced the asymptotic steady-streaming equations to a sequence of 1D boundary value problems on an annulus.
Solved these problems numerically to map how force varies with amplitude ratio, phase, and Reynolds number.
Validated the annulus proxy by comparing with direct simulations in a rectangular channel.
evidence_signal: For frequency ratio 2, the net force follows a closed-form dependence on phase and amplitude ratio, and channel simulations show net flux is directly proportional to annulus force across the tested parameter ranges.
watch_item: The force-to-flux proxy was tested only over the simulated parameter range, so device design should verify scaling before relying on it in new geometries or extreme operating conditions.
paper_title: Pumping by Two-frequency Steady Streaming: Impact of Amplitude Ratio and Phase
